metadata.scenario: A caregiver at a patient's home calls saying the patient is having difficulty breathing with oxygen saturation at 88. She asks if a nurse can come immediately. The receptionist tells her to call 911 first and dispatches a nurse. Tense, urgent call.

transcription.text: CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret, how can I help you? Hi, Margaret, this is Susan Garcia. I’m calling about my father. Hi, Susan. What seems to be the issue with your father? He has COPD, and right now he’s having difficulty breathing. I’m so sorry to hear that. Is he using his oxygen? Yes, but his oxygen saturation is only 88. It’s really low! Okay, Susan. That sounds urgent. Have you called 911 yet? No, I was hoping you could send a nurse right away. I understand, but it’s critical that you call 911 first. They can respond faster in emergencies. But I really need someone here! He’s really struggling! I get that, and I’ll dispatch a nurse immediately after you call 911. How long will it take for a nurse to arrive? It can take about 30 minutes, but that depends on the area and traffic. Okay, I’ll call 911 now. Please do, and stay on the line with me if you can. I’m calling now… (pause) Okay, I’ve called them. Great, I’m dispatching our registered nurse, Robert Davis, to your location. Thank you! Can he handle breathing treatments? Yes, Robert can administer treatments and monitor his condition. Will he be able to stay with my dad until help arrives? Yes, once he arrives, he will stay until medical help gets there. Thank you so much. I’m really worried. I understand, Susan. Your dad is in good hands. Are there any other concerns? Just that he’s been needing regular respiratory care. We can definitely help with that after this situation. What kind of services do you offer? We provide skilled nursing care, including medication management and respiratory treatments. How much does that cost? Our skilled nursing care ranges from $95 to $125 per visit. Okay, I’ll think about it once this is over. Sure, Susan. I’ll follow up with you after we resolve this. Thank you, Margaret. I really appreciate your help. You’re welcome. Stay calm, help is on the way. I will. Goodbye. Goodbye, Susan.
